record.paper_title: Open Questions in Cosmic-Ray Research at Ultrahigh Energies
record.original_question: Above roughly 10^19.4 eV, are the differences between the ultrahigh-energy cosmic-ray energy spectra measured by the Pierre Auger Observatory and the Telescope Array caused by experiment-specific systematic effects in energy reconstruction and calibration, or by astrophysical differences because the observatories view different parts of the sky?

evidence.quote: However, above this energy, larger differences remain present, which cannot be accounted for by an independent scaling of their reconstructed energies.

It will be important to understand whether this difference is caused by systematic uncertainties arising at the highest energies only, or whether it has an astrophysics origin related to seeing different parts of the sky.
As it is still too early to draw deﬁnite conclusions about the source of the differences, the joint working group will continue their studies.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Two large ground-based ultrahigh-energy cosmic-ray observatories independently measure the all-particle differential energy spectrum J(E) of cosmic rays at energies E ≳ 10^19 eV. One observatory is located in the Southern Hemisphere and views the sky in the declination band roughly −90° ≤ δ ≲ +45°; the other is located in the Northern Hemisphere and views roughly −16° ≲ δ ≤ +90°. Each observatory reconstructs primary energies via its own calibration chain (combining surface-detector signals with fluorescence-detector calorimetric measurements) and reports its spectrum with associated systematic uncertainties on the absolute energy scale.

When the two reported spectra J_A(E) and J_T(E) are compared above approximately E* = 10^19.4 eV, statistically significant differences remain even after applying any single global rescaling E → (1+α)E of one observatory's energy scale relative to the other (i.e., no energy-independent shift α can simultaneously reconcile the spectra in this regime, in particular reconciling the inferred flux-suppression energies).

Determine which of the following is the dominant cause of these residual differences above ~10^19.4 eV:

(a) experiment-specific systematic effects in energy reconstruction and calibration that depend on energy (so that the effective miscalibration grows with E and cannot be captured by a constant rescaling), or

(b) genuine astrophysical anisotropy of the ultrahigh-energy cosmic-ray sky, so that the two observatories sample intrinsically different flux distributions because their fields of view (declination bands) cover different regions of the celestial sphere.

Equivalently, decide whether the residual discrepancy is removed once one allows for an energy-dependent (but isotropic) inter-observatory energy-scale correction, or whether it persists when the comparison is restricted to the common declination band accessible to both instruments and therefore must be attributed to a declination-dependent astrophysical flux.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent joint Auger–Telescope Array working-group analyses (2024–2025) provide strong evidence that an energy-independent rescaling cannot eliminate the discrepancy above ~10^19.4 eV: the inferred suppression energies differ by ~42% (Auger ~48 EeV vs TA ~68 EeV, >3σ). Telescope Array has reported a declination-dependent feature in its spectrum, and updated comparisons indicate the tension is largely accounted for by a combination of an energy-dependent energy-scale mismatch and astrophysical (declination-dependent) effects, with proposed source-based explanations also under discussion. A definitive single-cause resolution has not yet been established, so the question is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Updated comparison of the UHECR energy spectra measured by the Pierre Auger Observatory and the Telescope Array
status_evidence.snippet: Significant tension in suppression energy: Auger E34=(48±3) EeV vs TA (68±5) EeV, >3σ; discrepancy in common bands interpretable as energy-dependent energy-scale shift.
status_evidence.claim: A constant rescaling cannot reconcile the spectra above the suppression; an energy-dependent shift is required.

status_evidence.title: Observation of Declination Dependence in the Cosmic Ray Energy Spectrum
status_evidence.snippet: Telescope Array reports declination dependence of the UHECR spectrum.
status_evidence.claim: Astrophysical (declination-dependent) contribution to the spectrum difference is supported by data.

status_evidence.title: Bright Cosmic-Ray Source as a Solution to Auger-TA Tensions
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes a bright nearby source as an astrophysical explanation of the Auger-TA tension.
status_evidence.claim: Astrophysical-origin explanations for the residual discrepancy remain actively proposed and not settled.
